correctness.rationale: For the repaired RESULT.md and SLOGAN.txt: all labelled pairs of total orders occur; homogeneity gives one base orbit per pair. Order-reversing and order-exchanging lifts exist by uniqueness of the homogeneous structure with this age. Their action on the order relations has kernel G and image W, so the closed finite coset union and inverse-image description agree with the finite type action. An order on n≥2 labels is never its reverse. The identity fixes (n!)² types, either no-reversal or double-reversal swaps fix n! each, and every other element fixes zero. The Burnside average yields the stated formula, including all subgroup rows; n=1 is separate. Equality partitions give the triangular Stirling transform. The six profile multiplicities 3,2,2,1,1,1 imply seven groups have nonunique profiles, not four as the literal frozen sentence says; four is the deficit of the number of scalar profiles from ten. The corrected finding says seven. On the four pair sign types the two one-order flips give different parallel matchings, the double flip and the double-flip/swap group give the same diagonal matching, S and the double-flip swap each give a distinct single merged pair, and exactly three groups act transitively. With the trivial partition this gives seven. The designated triple with orders 123 and 132 has trivial W-stabilizer since the orders are neither equal nor reversed, so its orbit alone identifies H. These arguments were reconstructed; the separate finite type enumeration found seven pair partitions, ten triple partitions and matched the recorded finite output without running the packaged script. The formula for all arities rests on the fixed-point proof, not on the finite checks.

value.rationale: On a natural full sublattice of a classical reduct classification, a researcher comparing oligomorphic growth with structural reconstruction needs to know whether two particular nonidentical closed groups remain indistinguishable even given every scalar count. The repaired result gives all such collisions, their exact multiplicities and first scalar distinguishing arity, not merely one coincidence or a numerical table requiring extrapolation. It explains the loss against the prior structural benchmark and provides a direct one-orbit comparison on the known action. The value is the sharp numerical information loss on an intrinsically defined family, not re-proving prior ternary separation.
